claims.text: A minor boron addition initially around 2 at.% will enhance icosahedral short-range order in phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloys.
Boron addition will produce denser atomic packing, particularly around phosphorus and boron atoms.
Incorporated boron promotes local atomic rearrangements that favor stable icosahedral short-range-order clusters.
Enhanced icosahedral short-range order reduces atomic mobility.
Reduced atomic mobility increases the kinetic barrier to crystallization.
An optimized minor boron addition will increase critical casting thickness relative to an otherwise comparable boron-free alloy.
An optimized minor boron addition will improve the critical cooling-rate metric relative to the boron-free alloy.
An optimized minor boron addition will raise the onset crystallization temperature relative to the boron-free alloy.
The benefits of boron addition depend on using an appropriate cooling rate.
The proposed effect is expected in alloys having high atomic-size mismatch and negative mixing enthalpies.
Boron concentrations above an optimal limit can promote competing crystalline boride phases.
Formation of competing crystalline borides will counteract the improvements in glass-forming ability and amorphous-state stability.

contradictions.description: The boundary predicts that sufficiently high boron levels may form borides without disproving the bounded optimum hypothesis, whereas the falsification rule broadly treats dominance of boride phases as falsifying. Borides at a deliberately excessive concentration such as 3 at.% would not by themselves falsify the claim unless they also preclude improvement throughout the proposed optimal range.
